Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Africa | National Germany can become Africa’s preferred business partner if it adapts to local needs – German Industry and Commerce in Ghana Source : Albert Kuzor 25 November 2026 3:00pm The Delegate of German Industry and Commerce in Ghana, Dr Michael Blank. ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The Delegate of German Industry and Commerce in Ghana, Dr Michael Blank, says Germany can strengthen its position as a preferred business partner for African countries if its companies adapt their investments to the continent's needs and priorities.
He said African countries were becoming increasingly confident in choosing their international business partners and expected investors to offer arrangements that support their economic development.
Speaking to JoyNews on the sidelines of the German-African Business Summit (GABS) 2026 in Accra, Dr Blank said Germany was not automatically the preferred partner for African countries but could earn that position through the right approach.
"They can choose their partners. And Germany is not necessarily number one, but we can be number one if we follow some rules and if we can adapt to the needs of the African partners," he said.
He identified support for local production as one of the key areas where German companies could respond to Africa's priorities.
According to him, helping African countries replace imports with locally manufactured goods would create opportunities for industrial growth.
He also urged German companies to invest in educating and training local workers alongside establishing production facilities.
"Another thing is maybe not only to produce here, but also to educate people and to train people. So these two things, if you combine it, can really make a difference," he added.
Dr Blank expressed confidence that more German companies would explore investment opportunities in Ghana and other African countries if they adopted such an approach.
